title: Client briefcase: priority list and light probe plan
content:
Purpose
A compact synthesis of recent field conversations (May–Jun 2026) focused on: predictable latency under mixed batch load, KV/prefix cache surprises, cost visibility for embeddings-heavy workloads, and a set of low-effort probes we can ship in the next 2–6 weeks to reduce customer pain.

Context summary (what customers are telling us)
- Latency vs. cost tradeoffs: Several mid-market customers say autoscaling/queueing behavior is opaque when they move from dev to prod; they see periodic 2–3x latency spikes during burst windows and are asking for clearer defaults or an "economy vs. steady" mode.
- KV cache warmup / cold-starts: Customers who use long conversational sessions report heavy token re-costing after a reconnect or worker swap. They want better cache persistence across short infra restarts or a user-visible cache health metric.
- Embeddings invoicing surprises: Data teams ran large re-embed jobs and hit unexpectedly high token/embedding unit bills because batched vs. streamed billing differences were unclear. They want a billing preview tool and an embedding-job cost estimator.
- Observability gaps: Platform teams want per-route trace anchors, cost-per-request attribution down to model-variant, and a clearer signal when a fallback was used (timestamp + reason).
- Private deployments: A few regulated customers flagged rollout friction—private control plane docs are thin on network pre-reqs and KMS rotation guidance.

Representative quotes
- "We thought Dedicated would buy us steady p99; instead latency stabilizes for 10–15m and then jumps—hard to diagnose." — Large fintech CTO
- "After a worker drain we saw a 90% re-cost on a 30k-token thread. Cache felt like it evaporated." — Healthtech infra lead
- "Embedding a dataset of 200k rows cost twice our estimate; the job kept switching to streaming and we lost batching efficiency." — Data eng manager

Priority list (compact) — ranked by ease of delivery vs. expected impact
1) Fallback and model-variant breadcrumb in traces (low effort, high clarity)
   - What: Add a small flag in request traces that records if a fallback occurred, which variant was used, and the rule triggered. Expose in Console under request detail.
   - Impact: Immediate reduction in support back-and-forth; quicker root cause for failover-related latency.
   - Rough effort: 1 sprint backend + small UX tile.

2) Embedding job cost preview + batch-vs-stream estimator (mid effort, high impact for data teams)
   - What: Console UI where customers can upload a sample CSV or provide row count + avg token estimate; we return a range for cost and recommended batch sizing. Link to SDK examples that show how to maximize batching.
   - Impact: Lower surprise billing, fewer escalations, more efficient use of hosted API.
   - Rough effort: 2–3 sprints cross-team (console + billing + SDK examples).

3) KV-cache "health" indicator + soft-warm API (low effort experimental)
   - What: Expose a small endpoint that returns cache hit ratio for a customer pool + an optional hint param that allows a short-lived prewarm operation for critical sessions. Document caveats.
   - Impact: Reduces perception of unpredictable re-costs for interactive apps; provides customers a mitigation path.
   - Rough effort: 2 sprints (serving runtime + docs).

4) Autoscaling visibility mode and a recommended default profile (mid effort)
   - What: Console toggle between "economy" and "steady" serving profiles. Economy favors lower unit cost and aggressive packing; steady favors latency SLOs (provision more warm capacity). Show expected p95/p99 and cost delta.
   - Impact: Prevents accidental prod surprises when teams copy dev configs; fewer support tickets about spikes.
   - Rough effort: 3 sprints (runtime + routing + console).

5) Private deploy preflight checklist & KMS rotation how-to (low effort docs + sample infra)
   - What: A short, prescriptive doc and a terraform module that codifies network rules, port lists, SKUs, and a KMS rotation script example.
   - Impact: Reduces onboarding time and trust friction for regulated customers.
   - Rough effort: 1 sprint (docs + infra sample).

Suggested 2‑week light probes (fast experiments to validate signal)
- Probe A: Trace breadcrumb rollout (implement in one region for a subset of customers). Measure reduction in support ticket time-to-resolution. Owner: Marco Ruiz.
- Probe B: Embedding cost preview MVP (CSV sample + quick cost estimate). Ship as beta to top 5 embedding customers. Owner: Jordan Kim.
- Probe C: Cache-health endpoint + CLI prewarm command (alpha). Give to two interactive-app customers to try. Owner: Priya Desai.

Customer-specific asks (annotated)
- Fintech X: wants guaranteed p99 under transactional bursts. Proposed: offer a dedicated steady profile and PS-led tuning. Follow-up: internal RFC for SLA language.
- HealthCo: wants persistent KV across short restarts. Proposed: experimental soft-warm + documentation on thread affinity and worker pinning.
- RetailerY: embedding job optimizer. Proposed: invite to embedding beta for cost-preview tool and custom batching script.

Unresolved questions / risks
- Will adding a cache prewarm API encourage unsafe client behavior (over-warming) that hurts multi-tenant fairness? Need SRE policy guardrails.
- Autoscaling toggle needs conservative defaults to avoid commercial SLA exposure — legal + sales should review any language implying hard SLAs.
- Billing estimator accuracy — if we publish wide ranges, it may reduce trust; if tight and wrong, will create new tickets. Start with conservative ranges and clear disclaimers.

Next actions (owner + due date)
- Build trace breadcrumb spec and PRD for the Console tile — Owner: Marco (due 2026-06-18).
- Draft Embedding-cost-preview MVP wireframes and sample SDK scripts — Owner: Jordan (due 2026-06-20).
- Prototype cache-health endpoint and run 2-customer alpha — Owner: Priya (due 2026-06-25).
- Legal review of autoscaling naming + SLA-adjacent copy — Owner: Aisha (due 2026-06-17).

Notes to self
- Keep probes opt-in and invite-only to limit blast radius.
- Capture before/after support ticket latency metrics to quantify impact.
- Add a short one-pager for sales that explains new profiles and expected tradeoffs (cost vs. latency).

Attachments / sample links (alpha)
- Linear ticket samples: INF-1342 (fallback trace anchoring), INF-1401 (embedding-cost-estimator).
- Console mock link: https://figma.redwood.ai/embed/xyz (internal)

End of brief

-- Aisha 
Quick pass, rough order-of-ops. Will iterate after Marco/Jordan/ Priya sync.
